<jats:p>
                    After the African origin of
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Homo sapiens</jats:italic>
                    , multiple dispersals radiated into Asia, yet the Saharo-Arabian archaeological record remains sparse. In this study, we report on ‘Uruq Aljelibah, a Middle Paleolithic site dated to ~125,000 years ago (marine isotope stage 5e) and located on the shore of Mundafan paleolake, Saudi Arabia. Levallois assemblages, refits, and megafaunal associations indicate in situ tool production and carcass processing. Stone tool residues, use-wear, and biomarkers reveal animal and plant processing, including palms, tubers, trees, and shrubs. Several points exhibit impact damage and poison residues (from
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Acokanthera schimperi</jats:italic>
                    ), indicating use as hafted weapon tips within composite hunting systems. Megafaunal remains include hippopotamus, buffalo, gazelle, ostrich, and camel, illuminating hominin use of freshwater and grassland ecosystems.
                  </jats:p>

items.abstract: Khor Abdullah is a strategically important marine area located between Iraq and Kuwait. Reconstructing the region's paleoenvironments and coastal evolution during the Quaternary period relies heavily on sea-level fluctuations, climatic conditions and neotectonics. This study examined two subbottom sediment cores (Cores 4 and 8), which were recovered from a depth of 40 m within the Grand Al-Faw Port region. Four primary faunal groups were identified foraminifera, ostracoda, mollusca and bryozoa—alongside notable sterile intervals lacking microfauna at multiple core depths. Benthic foraminifera were represented by six species, with the family Milliolidae dominating Core 4, which indicates turbid environments across supratidal, intertidal, and subtidal zones. Twelve ostracod species were identified, mostly corresponding to freshwater habitats. Furthermore, ten pelecypod and five gastropod species were documented, reflecting turbid and lagoonal environments. Bryozoa, meanwhile, occurred sporadically with low diversity. A distinct marine horizon at a depth of 28–30 m in Core 4 marks an Early Holocene marine transgression, which is interlayered with marsh deposits and evidence of subsequent marine regression. Textural analysis revealed that the core sediments predominantly consist of silt, muddy sand and sandy silt. According to the hydrodynamic conditions diagram, most sediment samples fall within the quietest environment. This explains the absence of fauna at most depths, as the soil texture at these depths is unsuitable for habitation by fauna.

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:italic>Eudocimus ruber</jats:italic>
                    (Linnaeus, 1758), commonly known as the scarlet ibis, is a wading bird widely distributed throughout northern South America and along the Brazilian coast. However, detailed information on the ocular morphology of this species remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to perform a multimodal morphological characterization of the eye and its associated structures in
                    <jats:italic>E. ruber</jats:italic>
                    . Eight specimens were used, and the heads were subjected to radiographic and computed tomographic examinations, followed by gross anatomical dissection, three‐dimensional reconstruction, histological processing, and scanning electron microscopy. Gross anatomy revealed laterally positioned, flat‐shaped eyes, eight extraocular muscles, a well‐developed Harderian gland, and a pleated pecten oculi. Radiographic, tomographic, and three‐dimensional analyses enabled visualization of the scleral ring and its anatomical position within the orbit. Histological examination identified the fibrous, vascular, and retinal tunics, including the scleral ossicles, scleral cartilage, ciliary body, iris, 10‐layered retina, annular pad, pleated pecten oculi, Harderian gland, eyelids, and third eyelid. The scleral ossicles followed the type A overlap pattern according to the Lemmrich convention. The ocular morphology of
                    <jats:italic>E. ruber</jats:italic>
                    was generally consistent with that described in other avian species, with interspecific variation observed in several anatomical features. These findings expand the available anatomical knowledge of Threskiornithidae and provide a basis for future comparative studies of avian ocular morphology.
                  </jats:p>

items.summary: 《红鹮眼部形态学分析》：该研究对红鹮的眼部及相关结构进行多模态形态学表征，采用X射线、计算机断层扫描、大体解剖、三维重建、组织学处理和扫描电子显微镜观察八例标本，描述了侧位扁平眼、八条眼外肌、发达的哈氏腺、褶皱状栉膜及巩膜环等结构，发现其眼部形态与其他鸟类基本一致但存在种间差异，可为进一步比较研究鸟类眼部形态提供解剖学基础。
items.title: Morphological analysis of the eye of Eudocimus ruber (Linnaeus, 1758)
